set.layering_notes: Fresno County splits housing work three ways: the Department of Public Works and Planning, Community Development Division (ComDev) runs the Urban County HUD programs, PLHA and the annual Affordable Housing Development NOFO; the County Administrative Office's new Office of Housing and Homelessness (OHH, created November 18, 2025) administers HHAP, the Continuum of Care and Transitional Rent and is absorbing housing programs from Behavioral Health and ComDev (Phase 2 approved November 3, 2026); and the Department of Behavioral Health co-applies for Homekey+ and NPLH and funds BHSA housing. Fresno Housing (the joint City and County Housing Authorities) is the dominant developer and voucher source. The City of Fresno and Clovis are separate entitlements with their own programs (Pass 3). fresnocountyca.gov and fresnohousing.org open normally; Board records are on fresnocounty.legistar.com and the Legistar web API client 'fresnocounty'. Fresno is one of the few counties in this database putting BHSA into capital (about $6.1 million a year) and into long operating subsidies ($287,000 a year for 30 years at Victory Village, $15.3 million over 20 years at Sendero Commons). Tenant-based subsidies serve 869 people in year one rising to 1,049, 372 units a year. Capital money has gone first to Fresno Housing (Victory Village) and to the Homekey+ project in Sanger. Source is the revised 2026-2029 Integrated Plan PDF; budget figures from the Integrated Plan Budget attachment to Board file 26-0538 and the Victory Village resolution (file 26-0585). Audit 2026-11-08: classed as grant because the BHSA Integrated Plan funds housing capital (Capital Development Projects $6,098,789 to $6,118,094 a year) and rental and operating subsidies for housing; the Victory Village resolution (No. 26-251) is a conditional capital commitment and operating subsidy, and the loan or grant form of the capital will be set in the enforceable funding agreement after a 9% award.

set.typical_award_size: Location-based reduction of development impact fees under the Impact Fee Reduction Incentive Program (Resolution 2022-060): Infill Area fees 25% below Expansion Area and City Center fees 50% below. 2022 multifamily impact fees per unit: $17,569 Expansion Area, $13,177 Infill Area, $8,785 City Center. Regional Transportation Mitigation fee is reduced for affordable units ($821 per affordable multifamily unit). Development impact fee deferral program (approved May 26, 2015): applicant pays a nonrefundable 20% of impact fees at building permit application and the remaining 80% before final inspection. Housing Element Program 7 also commits to continued fee reductions and deferrals for affordable and special-needs projects and lists reduced water and wastewater connection fees as a flexible standard.
set.audit_note: Housing Element Appendix 1L supports the area reductions, 2022 fee amounts, the 2015 deferral terms and Resolution 2022-060; it does not mention Resolution 2019-009. reedley.ca.gov failed TLS handshake on 2026-11-08 so the current fee schedule and any December 2025 fee revision under Program 17 could not be checked. Prevailing wage: Labor Code 1720(b)(4) treats reduced or waived fees as public funds, but leginfo returned 403 and no City or DIR rule on these fee programs was read, so the trigger stays unclear.

reason: Housing Element supports the fee figures but the city site could not be opened to confirm the current schedule and no stated prevailing wage rule for these fee programs could be read.
